feedback.Physical Object: Included — A robotic arm is a discrete, bounded electromechanical unit.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — Fully engineered and constructed by human design.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Included — Typically inspired by the form or articulation of biological limbs.
feedback.Powered: Included — Operates using electrical, pneumatic, or hydraulic energy.
feedback.Structural: Included — Composed of rigid segments and joints that form a load-bearing frame.
feedback.Observable: Included — Visibly tracks motion; its activity is monitored during operation.
feedback.Physical Medium: Included — Composed of tangible, physical materials and mechanisms.
feedback.Active: Included — Continuously moves, responds to input, and drives effectors.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Engineered for manipulation, automation, and controlled movement.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Included — Produces changes in position, force, or configuration of the environment.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Included — Interprets commands from programs, sensors, or control interfaces.
feedback.State-Transforming: Included — Changes internal joint angles and actuator states during motion.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Included — Often controlled by, or collaborates with, human operators.
feedback.System-integrated: Included — Usually part of an industrial, medical, or research automation system.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Included — Capable of executing complex motion sequences independently once programmed.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Robotic arms are modular; most systems can substitute or bypass them.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Sends status messages, sensor data, and indicator signals to humans or systems.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Constrained by control rules, safety bounds, and motion profiles.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Made up of modular actuators, joints, and control electronics.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Motion execution and coordination depend on temporal sequencing.
feedback.Symbolic: Excluded — Not a representational or symbolic entity.
feedback.Meta: Excluded — Does not manage or represent its own logic or abstraction.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Must comply with industrial safety and robotic standards (e.g., ISO/TS 15066).
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Widely used in manufacturing, logistics, and medical robotics.
feedback.Politicised: Included — A focus of economic and labor-policy debate related to automation.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Raises concerns around labor displacement, surveillance, and human-machine cooperation.
feedback.Social Construct: Excluded — Defined by engineering, not cultural agreement.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Excluded — Not classified or governed by an institutional authority.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Excluded — Not tied to personal, professional, or cultural identity.
feedback.Ritualised: Excluded — Not used in symbolic or ceremonial behavior.

encoding_notes: This encoding captures the robotic arm as a modular, powered, and biomimetic actuator governed by structured logic and temporal coordination. It is both economically and ethically significant, and actively communicates its state, warranting inclusion of the Signalling trait. Final UHT code: FFFE721D.
